conviction_note: Near-balanced: the one live question is whether the end-3Q El Nino reassessment management promised produces a second provisioning top-up beyond what a ~S/2.0bn consensus implies (ENFEN odds worsened after the Q2 booking; BBVA Peru's Q3 impairments rose), set against a de-risked tape (-6.4% in 20 days, low short interest), firm non-primary GDP and a hawkish-hold BCRP that supports NIM; the stock sold its last beat (1Q26 -3.5%) and the Nov 17 strategic update is outside the window and likely holds back the medium-term story, so p_up 48 on an abs move of 3.8, rebuilt from confirmed releases (last four: +0.7, -3.3, -3.5, +3.0) and set above that median because the hunters run small, while the 6.47% option figure sits on a 37%-of-mid spread.
bar: 3Q26 EPS consensus $7.51 (finviz/Zacks-style preview dated 2026-11-02, https://finviz.com/news/413767/credicorp-brings-raised-targets-into-an-el-nino-provisioning-test-as-shares-hug-lows) and $7.55 (EarningsWhispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/BAP); the two agree within 0.5%. The revenue consensus of $1.84bn (-8.6% YoY) quoted in the same preview is described there as 'hard to reconcile' and is not used. Company guide: FY2026 ROE ~19.5% with an upward bias, loan growth ~12%, CoR 1.7-2.1%, fee growth high teens, NIM toward the high end (2Q26 6-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001001290/000114036126033379/ef20080305_ex99-1.htm). 1H26 ROE was 21.2%, so the FY guide survives a sizeable 3Q top-up. Hunter's own inference, not a source: $7.51 x ~79.3m shares x ~3.40 PEN/USD comes to about S/2.02bn of Q3 net income, against S/1.98bn in 2Q26, which itself carried S/106m of El Nino provisions.
positioning_check: Short interest is low and not crowded: about 1.1m shares, 1.6% of float, up 18.9% on the prior report (MarketBeat via search, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/BAP/short-interest/, Oct-Nov 2026); ShortSqueeze 1.25m shares with 3.5 days to cover as of 2026-09-23 (https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=BAP); Benzinga 2.3% of float on 2026-10-14 (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/BAP/sentiment). ORTEX's 0.14% / 137.9 days figure is inconsistent with the rest and ignored. Skew: the baseline rejected the 25-delta skew (-41.6 vol points, implausible) and put/call OI is 0.97 on only 572 contracts, so the options carry no directional statement. Tape: -6.41% over 20 days, -11.2% from the 52-week high, and on 2026-11-02 it sat just above its post-2Q low ($346.54), with bullish sentiment down to 35.7% from 46.5% (finviz preview). It closed at $347.93 on 2026-11-06 and was sealed at $357.39 intraday on 2026-11-09.

findings.finding: Credicorp booked about S/106m of El Nino provisions in 2Q26 (27bp of CoR; reported CoR 1.9% against an underlying 1.6%) and said it would reassess El Nino expected losses at the end of 3Q or start of 4Q. Since then ENFEN's outlook for the Dec 2026-Mar 2027 peak has worsened: communique No.14 (~early August) gave 43% strong / 41% extraordinary, No.16 of 2026-09-14 gave 48% extraordinary / 45% strong and made extraordinary the most likely magnitude for Sep 2026-Jan 2027, and an 18 October report says the event runs into autumn 2027. A second top-up is therefore more likely than not in this release, and its size against an EPS bar of $7.51 that implies Q3 net income of roughly S/2.0bn (about Q2's level) is the line this print turns on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Provisioning and cost of risk drive this name's prints. 4Q25 (CoR 1.8%, EPS miss): -3.3% on 2026-02-13. 1Q26 (record ROE 21.1% on lower provisions, EPS beat ~4.6%): sold, -3.5% on 2026-05-15. 2Q26 (S/106m El Nino top-up, in line, medium-term ROE raised to ~22%): +3.0% on 2026-08-14. Closes are from the Yahoo chart API.
findings.why_not_priced: The risk is known: the Nov 2 preview names El Nino provisioning as 'the key uncertainty' and the stock is down 6.6% since the last report. What is not visibly priced is the size. A consensus that already carried a large second top-up would show Q3 EPS below Q2's $7.29, yet $7.51 is above it. Partly priced, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: ENFEN probabilities: https://caretas.pe/nacional/el-nino-costero-costa-peruana-tendria-temperaturas-hasta-5-c-por-encima-de-lo-normal-y-lluvias-mas-intensas/ (2026-09-15) and https://panamericana.pe/nacionales/472835-nino-costero-extenderia-mayo-2027-magnitud-fuerte-extraordinaria (communique 14). The 'reassess at end 3Q/early 4Q' statement is from the 2Q call, via https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/credicorp-q2-earnings-call-highlights. Weather-to-provision transmission is inference; only the company's own reassessment commitment is a primary document.

findings.finding: A peer that reported after Credicorp last spoke: in BBVA's 3Q26 report (6-K for October 2026), BBVA Peru's quarterly profit fell 28.6% QoQ to EUR 81m, 'mainly as a result of higher impairment on financial assets'. Its cumulative cost of risk rose 18bp to 1.43%, while loans grew 8.1% year to date and consumer loans 11.0%. The filing contrasts strong domestic demand with El Nino damage to primary sectors. This is direct evidence that provisioning rose across Peruvian banks in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same line as finding 1 (provisions/CoR): -3.3%, -3.5% and +3.0% on the last three prints.
findings.why_not_priced: BBVA Peru is a line inside a Spanish group's report that BAP's US-listed holders rarely read. Had it reached BAP estimates, the consensus would sit below Q2's EPS rather than above it. The Peru figures are snippet_only: the full 6-K fetch truncated before the South America chapter, and the quoted sentences come from the search result citing the filing. BBVA itself says the prior quarter's impairments were 'particularly low', which partly explains the QoQ swing, so it is sized below finding 1.
findings.independence: This is a different company and document from finding 1, but it bears on the same question (higher Q3 provisioning in Peru), so the two should not be read as two independent confirmations of one fact. Macro context: BBVA Research on El Nino as the main drag, https://www.bbvaresearch.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Peru_Economic_Outlook.pdf.

findings.finding: Peru's quarter was firm outside the primary sectors. GDP grew 3.56% in July and 3.2% in August 2026 (INEI/MEF), with construction +10.3% and commerce +6.9% while fishing fell 17-27% and mining fell. The BCRP trimmed its 2026 growth forecast to 3.2% only because of El Nino. On 2026-10-22 President Fujimori announced a S/18bn injection for 2027. All of this supports the raised ~12% loan-growth and high-teens fee guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan and fee growth beats have not been paid on their own. 1Q26 was a record quarter and the stock fell 3.5%. 2Q26 (+13.1% YoY loans, guidance raised) rose 3.0%, mostly on the medium-term ROE target.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. These are public monthly series, and the loan-growth guide was already raised in August. If the market expected loan growth to come in short, consensus EPS would sit below Q2's, and it sits above. Macro-to-company transmission, so sized small.
findings.independence: Fujimori S/18bn: https://andina.pe/agencia/noticia-president-keiko-fujimori-announces-s18-billion-injection-for-2027-to-boost-perus-economy-1096975.aspx (2026-10-22). BBVA Peru's loans +8.1% YTD and consumer +11.0% (finding 2's filing) point the same way for volumes.

findings.finding: Rates and FX in the quarter favoured the margin. The BCRP held its policy rate at 4.25% on 2026-10-07 for a thirteenth month with a hiking bias, surprising a market that expected a hike, because inflation is above its 1-3% target range (about 4% at end-Q2, near 5% forecast for year-end). Higher-for-longer rates support the NIM, which the company already guided toward the high end. The sol weakened from ~3.36 to ~3.44 per USD in late September, which helps FX trading income (as election volatility did in Q2) and slightly lowers USD-translated EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM has improved for several quarters (2Q26 6.63%, +5bp QoQ). The +3.0% reaction to 2Q26 is the only recent print where the margin was a headline.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. NIM 'toward the high end' was guided in August, and public rate decisions are in every model. The residual is that the hike-bias hold extends the high-rate period, which may not be fully in 4Q/2027 NIM expectations. Small.
findings.independence: FX path: https://tucambista.pe/noticias/dolares-a-soles-29-setiembre-2026 (BCRP close 3.4410 on 2026-09-29). Hold and surprise: https://infomercado.pe/bcrp-mantiene-su-tasa-en-4-25-y-sorprende-a-un-mercado-que-esperaba-un-alza/.

findings.finding: Credicorp hosts its 2026 Strategic Update on 2026-11-17, eight days after this print and outside the window, on 'maturity, monetization and operating leverage' of the ecosystem (Yape at 8.9% of risk-adjusted revenue in 2Q26). Medium-term targets and 2027 framing will likely be held for it, so this release and the Nov 10 call probably carry less forward information than a normal print. That damps the reaction in either direction rather than signing it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last guidance surprise (medium-term ROE raised to ~22% from ~19.5% in 2Q26) came with +3.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: The date is public. What is not priced is its effect on this window, and it argues for a smaller absolute move than the 6.47% option figure, which rests on a 37%-of-mid ATM spread. No directional content.
findings.independence: The Nov 2 preview also says management 'may hold back strategic detail' for Nov 17: https://finviz.com/news/413767/credicorp-brings-raised-targets-into-an-el-nino-provisioning-test-as-shares-hug-lows.

findings.finding: Positioning is de-risked into the print: -6.4% over 20 days, just above the post-2Q low on Nov 2, bullish sentiment down to 35.7% from 46.5%, 21% below the ~$427-432 average analyst target (14 analysts Buy), and short interest only 1.6-2.3% of float. The El Nino worry has been sold ahead of the release, so a top-up in the S/100m range that keeps the FY ROE guide is unlikely to take the stock to new lows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Into 2Q26 the stock had run +31% YTD and still rose 3.0% on an in-line print. Into 1Q26 it fell 3.5% on a beat. No clean prior case of a de-risked setup.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The finding is that the drawdown already reflects the El Nino concern that findings 1-2 raise, so the two partly offset. Sized small because it is a positioning read, not a document.
